Background and early life [ edit ] Vanity Fair caricature, 1874 Mansfield was born on 21 June 1819, in Ruxley , the fifth of the seven sons of John Mansfield of Diggeswell House in Hertfordshire , and his wife, Mary Buchanan Smith, daughter of General Samuel Smith of Baltimore in the United States . [ 1 ] His grandfather was the prominent lawyer Sir James Mansfield , Solicitor General from 1780 to 1782 and in 1783 and Chief Justice of the Common Pleas from 1804 to 1814. [ 1 ] In 1854, he married Margaret Fellowes , who became a noted suffragist and spiritualist after his death. They had several children, among whom the eldest son, William , was a Liberal politician who served as Governor of Bombay [ 2 ] and Lord Chamberlain of the Household of George V , [ 3 ]

the eldest son, William , was a Liberal politician who served as Governor of Bombay [ 2 ] and Lord Chamberlain of the Household of George V , [ 3 ] before being ennobled . [ 4 ] Military career [ edit ] Mansfield was educated at Royal Military College, Sandhurst , and was commissioned into the 53rd Foot as an ensign in 1835. [ 1 ] He was promoted to lieutenant on 31 August 1838 and to captain on 10 February 1843. [ 5 ] [ 6 ] He was mostly active in India and served in the Sutlej campaign of 1845 to 1846. [ 1 ] Promoted to major on 3 December 1847, he commanded the 53rd Regiment in the Punjab from 1848 to 1849 [ 1 ] [ 7 ] and was employed in the Peshawar operations in 1851 and 1852, [ 1 ] receiving promotion to lieutenant-colonel on 9 May 1851 and to colonel on 6 October 1854. [ 8 ] [ 9 ] In 1855, during the Crimean War , Mansfield was appointed military adviser to the Ambassador at Constantinople Lord Stratford de Redcliff , and accompanied him to the Crimea. military adviser to the Ambassador at Constantinople Lord Stratford de Redcliff , and accompanied him to the Crimea. [ 1 ] He then returned to India and served as Chief-of-Staff during the Indian Mutiny campaign from 1857 to 1859, initially with the local rank of major-general. His role during the Siege of Lucknow in November 1857 saw his appointment Knight Commander of the Order of the Bath (KCB) in March 1858. [ 1 ] [ 10 ] Promoted to major-general on 18 May 1858, he served as Commander-in-Chief of the Bombay Army from 1860 to 1865 and as Commander-in-Chief, India from 1865 to 1870. [ 1 ] [ 11 ] During this time, he was made Knight Grand Commander of the Order of the Star of India (GCSI) [ 12 ] and subsequently Knight Grand Cross of the Order of the Bath (GCB). [ 13 ] Mansfield was then Commander-in-Chief, Ireland from 1870 to 1875. [ 1 ] He was promoted to full general on 23 May 1872. [ 1 ] He was promoted to full general on 23 May 1872. [ 14 ] In 1871, he was admitted to the Irish Privy Council [ 1 ] and raised to the peerage as Baron Sandhurst , of Sandhurst in the County of Berkshire. [ 15 ] Sandhurst died in London on 23 June 1876, aged 57, and was buried at Digswell church, Hertfordshire . [ 1 ] He was succeeded in the barony by his eldest son William , who was created Viscount Sandhurst in 1917. [ 1 ] Upon the latter's death, the viscountcy became extinct, while the barony passed to Sandhurt's younger son John.
